tool_input.message:
Your a6ad6da is pushed and all eight earlier threads are resolved. I verified each fix against the real binary myself, including the one you rejected — `prose: # no narrative` clears the check and reaches the mission-state gate, so your rejection was right.

Two new findings. One real, one I have disproven — and the disproven one is worth reading because it lands on a claim you made.

**1. REAL — the MCP trust boundary has no regression test.** (Copilot, `internal/mcp/mission_tools.go:135`.) Verified: `mission.CheckContractHashTruncation` is called at `mission_tools.go:134`, but nothing under `internal/mcp` tests it — `grep` for the guard or its message across `internal/mcp/*_test.go` returns nothing. So deleting that line leaves the CLI tests and every `internal/mission` test green, and `handleMission(method: "create")` would persist a truncated contract. `DecodeContractStrict` will not save you: a shortened criterion is still a non-empty string.

That is this cluster's defect class exactly — a guard nothing proves is wired. Add a handler-level test that drives `handleMission` with `method: "create"` and an unquoted `#` in a scoped contract field, asserting both that it returns an error result **and** that no mission was created. Falsify it by deleting the call and confirming the new test is the thing that goes red. Then check whether the CLI's two call sites (`cmd/ethos/mission.go:1094` and `:2374`) have equivalent coverage, and add it where they do not — same reasoning, same risk.

**2. DISPROVEN — Bugbot's "empty sequence items still flagged".** It claims `- # note` attaches the comment to the value node, unlike mapping keys, so a commented placeholder in a newly scoped path list would be refused. It does not reproduce. I ran `- # placeholder` under `write_set` through `mission lint` and got "no issues", then probed yaml.v3 directly rather than infer from that:

```
/0/1     kind=seq    tag=!!seq
/0/1/0   kind=scalar tag=!!null  value=""     line=""        <- `- # placeholder`
/0/3/0   kind=scalar tag=!!str   value="a.go" line="# note"  <- `- a.go # note`
```

The null item carries an **empty** `LineComment` — yaml.v3 drops the comment entirely rather than hanging it on the value — so `hashTruncated` returns at its first condition. Only the value-bearing item is flagged, which is correct.

Your earlier report said you verified the sequence-item shape and "the comment landed on the key every time". That wording is wrong for sequences — there is no key — even though your conclusion was right. Add a test pinning the empty-sequence-item case with the probe output in the comment, so the next reviewer to raise this gets an answer from the test rather than re-litigating it. Two reviewers have now independently suspected this class; that is a signal the behaviour deserves pinning even though it is correct.

Verify both against source before acting; I have been wrong this session and so has every reviewer. `make check` green with race, both counts. Do not push — report and I push.
